title: Enterprise network exemption workflow and reversible upgrade playbook for Private/VPC/on‑prem requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We're seeing an increase in complex Private/VPC/on‑prem requests where customers (finance, healthcare, gov) cannot meet our standard inbound/outbound networking assumptions (no egress, strict proxy, constrained NAT, or deep packet inspection). These requests often stall during scoping because engineering needs more reproducible artifacts and the upgrade / patching steps are perceived as risky by customers. This ticket scopes and ships a productized intake rubric plus a small operational playbook that enables: 1) consistent prioritization scoring for network exemptions, 2) a minimal set of artifacts we require from customers up front, and 3) a reversible upgrade/rollback path and communication playbook for kernel/OS/container/image upgrades in airgapped environments.
goals: Create a 10‑item intake rubric to quickly score network compatibility and triage priority
Define required customer artifacts (network diagrams, egress policies, proxy certs, upgrade windows)
Ship a 5‑step reversible upgrade playbook for private deployments including automated probes and rollback hooks
Standardize the communication template for SRE/SE/PM interactions during preflight and upgrade windows
Reduce average intake->kickoff time for high‑risk network requests from 21 days to under 7 days
acceptance_criteria: Intake rubric doc published in Confluence with scoring weights and example customer profiles
Checklist UI spec for Console intake form drafted and approved by design
Rollback playbook validated in two internal staging clusters (one with NAT, one airgapped)
Support runbook (SE/SRE steps + contact matrix) reviewed and accepted by SRE and Solutions
Two pilot customers successfully onboarded using the new rubric and playbook
proposed_solution_summary: Deliver a small, repeatable product + ops artifact set: (A) a 10‑point scoring rubric (network topology, egress, proxy auth, cert management, OS patch policy, maintenance window tolerance, KMS/HSM reachability, required ports, image transfer method, and rollback tolerance), (B) an intake template to capture required artifacts, (C) an automated preflight probe suite (runnable client side or as a one‑time remote probe), and (D) a reversible upgrade playbook with version pinning, staged rollout, automated health checks, and fast rollback hooks.
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep the rubric conservative to reduce surprise work for engineering; some medium scores will still require an eng scoping call.
- Building an integrated probe in Console is higher effort; initial rollout will be a downloadable probe script plus a results uploader tile in Console.
- Airgapped customers may never allow live telemetry; the intake should support uploading probe outputs and signed manifests.
- We will not attempt to automate complex kernel upgrades in the first iteration; the playbook focuses on container image, runtime, and config changes with explicit fallbacks for kernel/OS where required.
required_artifacts_from_customer: Network diagram showing NAT/eBGP/proxies and cloud onramps
Firewall/ACL matrix with port ranges and CIDR lists
Maintenance window availability and change control policy
KMS/HSM access details and whether remote key wrapping is allowed
Image transfer method (airgap bundle, pull-through proxy, signed image server)
Proxy certs and list of TLS interception appliances (if any)
Contact matrix for operators and escalation thresholds
